name: Socrata Open Data API (state and city portals)
publisher: Tyler Technologies, deployed by hundreds of governments
description: The engine behind most US state and city open data portals - data.ny.gov, data.cityofchicago.org, data.seattle.gov, healthdata.gov and hundreds more. Every dataset gets the same REST interface with a SQL-like query language (SoQL), so one client works against all of them. With the federal catalogue's API down, this is the practical route to US public-sector data.

license.name: per-portal; most are public domain or CC-BY

access.auth_note: anonymous access works and is throttled by IP; a free app token raises the limit and is passed as X-App-Token
access.rate_limit: strict but unpublished for anonymous callers; generous with an app token
access.pagination: $limit and $offset, or $order plus a keyset filter for large walks

fields: Every dataset has a 4x4 id like pmsa-f2ss
/resource/<4x4>.json is the data; /api/views/<4x4>.json is the metadata

probes.description: Search across every Socrata portal at once

gotchas.trap: The default $limit is 1,000, not 'all'. A loop that never sets $limit silently analyses the first thousand rows.
gotchas.fix: Set $limit explicitly and page with $offset, or use the /rows.csv export for the whole table.

gotchas.trap: $where uses SoQL, not SQL - string literals are single-quoted and dates want ISO with no timezone suffix.
gotchas.fix: Test the filter in the portal's own query builder first.

gotchas.trap: Anonymous requests share an IP throttle, so a fast loop from an office network gets 429s that look like your fault.
gotchas.fix: Register a free app token and send X-App-Token.
